tagline.text: A road tunnel through Mt. Pico de Loro to the western coast

location.label: Location
location.text: Maragondon–Ternate boundary, Cavite, on the Ternate–Nasugbu Road (Tourism Road)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱300~1,000 (round-trip public transport and snacks, per person per day)

children.text: Kaybiang Tunnel is a road tunnel about 300 m long that cuts through Mt. Pico de Loro (Palay-Palay range). It opened in July 2013 and links Ternate in Cavite with Nasugbu in Batangas. There is no entrance fee and it can be passed 24 hours a day (per a 2019 blog), but since March 2021 the Cavite provincial government has declared the tunnel area a 'no tourism zone' that bans parking, selfies and loitering nearby, so check the current rules locally. It is known for its drive and the western coastal views beyond the tunnel.
Kaybiang Tunnel is a road tunnel on the Ternate–Nasugbu Road (Tourism Road), which crosses the Mts. Palay-Palay–Mataas-na-Gulod Protected Landscape at the western end of Cavite. It is about

long, a figure given consistently by Wikipedia and several travel blogs. The tunnel passes through the northern flank of Mt. Pico de Loro (Mt. Palay-Palay); one end opens toward the sea on the Ternate, Cavite side, and the other leads to the coast on the Nasugbu, Batangas side. Planning is said to have begun in 1994, construction took place around 2009, and the tunnel officially opened in July 2013.

The tunnel became well known because it greatly shortened the trip from Manila to the western Batangas coast, such as Nasugbu and Calatagan. Several blogs say the trip that once took about 4 hours via Tagaytay dropped to roughly 1.5 to 2 hours after the tunnel road opened (about 4 hours to about 2 hours at the 2013 opening, and a 2021 guide to the PITX bus also says 1.5 to 2 hours). Treat this only as a rough guide, because actual time varies widely with traffic. Today it is both a gateway to coastal resorts such as Hamilo Coast (Pico de Loro resort), Punta Fuego, Tali Beach and Canyon Cove, and a favorite drive for weekend riders and cycling groups.

The appeal lies less in the tunnel itself than in what surrounds it. Many reviews say the inside has no lighting, which gives it a dark, cool atmosphere, and when you come out the other side the sea opens up with views of Limbones, Carabao and El Fraile islands. A blog mentions a climb above the tunnel entrance with a Virgin Mary statue, and there is a sari-sari store by the road where you can buy drinks and snacks. There are no restrooms or restaurants, so prepare in advance.

It is also worth knowing that the location is described inconsistently. Many travel listings give the address as Ternate (Santa Mercedes), but Wikipedia and OpenStreetMap place the tunnel in Maragondon. The road runs along the boundary of the two municipalities, so either name points to the same tunnel. This guide classifies the region as Cavite.

blocks.title: One of the longest road tunnels in the Philippines

children.text: Many articles describe it as "the longest road tunnel in the Philippines" at about
. However, there is only a comparison saying Manila's Boni-Pioneer tunnel is about 280 m, and no official ranking was found, so "one of the longest" is the accurate way to put it.

blocks.title: Passing through a dark, unlit tunnel

children.text: Several reviews say the tunnel has no lighting. It is dark from entrance to exit even in daytime, so cars need their headlights on, and many reviewers say this is what makes the passage feel special.

blocks.title: Western coastal views beyond the exit

children.text: When you come out on the Nasugbu side, the view opens toward the sea with Limbones, Carabao and El Fraile islands. Many people take photos on the shoulder and at viewpoints, so wait for a gap in traffic and shoot safely.
The tunnel sits on a Tourism Road section about
6 km
long, with a winding climb up the mountain followed by a descent along the sea. Motorcycle and cycling groups come here often on weekends.
A blog records a footpath above the tunnel entrance leading to a Virgin Mary statue. I could not confirm how well the path is maintained, so check its condition on site and do not push yourself.

blocks.title: A route that connects to Mt. Pico de Loro

children.text: The mountain the tunnel passes through is Mt. Pico de Loro itself. Hiking it usually follows the entry procedure on the Hamilo Coast side, and it combines well with a light stop at the tunnel to make a one-day plan.

blocks.title: Access road to resorts and coves

children.text: This is the gateway to coastal resorts and coves such as Hamilo Coast (Pico de Loro resort), Punta Fuego, Tali Beach, Maya-Maya and Canyon Cove. The tunnel is said to have made this area much faster to reach.

items.title: Half-day drive
items.subtitle: Leave Manila, see the tunnel and head home

children.text: Leave Manila (Macapagal Avenue, for example) and head south toward Las Piñas, Bacoor, Imus and Dasmariñas. These stretches are heavily congested, so leaving early is the biggest tip.
Pass Trece Martires, Naic and Maragondon and climb toward Ternate. There may be road works or weekend traffic along the way, so check your map app.
Arrive at Kaybiang Tunnel. Turn on your headlights, drive through slowly, and take photos safely from the shoulder near the entrance. Buy a drink at the roadside store.
Come out of the tunnel and look at the view toward Limbones, Carabao and El Fraile islands from the viewpoint on the Nasugbu side.
If you have time, have lunch at a resort restaurant toward Hamilo Coast or Tali Beach, or turn back the way you came. Check access and fees with the resort in advance.
Set off back toward Manila before the return traffic builds up.

One blog says that by public transport you can take a Nasugbu-bound bus from PITX that passes along the tunnel road, but there is no clearly designated stop for getting off to see the tunnel and boarding again. Ask the driver on the spot.

items.title: Overnight coastal combination
items.subtitle: The tunnel together with the western Batangas coast

children.text: Leave Manila. Enjoy the tunnel and the Tourism Road scenery as you cross toward Nasugbu.
After the tunnel, enjoy the coastal view and a rest.
Have lunch, swim and relax at a coastal resort such as Tali Beach, Maya-Maya or Canyon Cove.
Check in to your lodging while watching the sunset. Many people stay on the western Batangas coast, such as Calatagan and Matabungkay.
Look into the entry procedure for Mt. Pico de Loro or enjoy a nearby beach, then drive back through the tunnel.
Some blog reports describe a same-day round trip taking more than 9 hours. A night in Batangas or Tagaytay is more relaxed.

items.title: From Manila by car or motorcycle

children.text: The common route runs through Cavite. From Dasmariñas it continues through Trece Martires, Naic and Maragondon toward Ternate. Search "Kaybiang Tunnel" in your map app.
The tunnel is less than 100 km from Manila in a straight line, but travel time varies greatly with traffic. One article says about
2 hours
, while another reports a same-day round trip of more than 9 hours.
Unlike the route to Nasugbu via Tagaytay, this road climbing from the Cavite side lets the tunnel save time.
Reviews say small-displacement motorcycles are not allowed on some highway sections, so check your route.
According to a blog, Nasugbu-bound buses from PITX pass along the tunnel road (about 1.5 to 2 hours), with a fare of about
one way per a 2019 blog (a recent fare could not be confirmed). Fares and service change, so confirm on the spot.
Getting off at the tunnel to look around and then flagging another bus in the same direction is not a reliable method, because there may be no designated stop.

Public transport near the tunnel is limited, so a private car, rental car or chartered van is more convenient. You can also look for a tricycle or shared ride up from Ternate town, but negotiate the fare on the spot.
Reviews say mobile signal and battery can become a problem near the tunnel, so bring a power bank.

The tunnel road was open 24 hours with no entrance fee per a 2019 blog, but since March 19, 2021 the Cavite provincial government has declared the area a 'no tourism zone': parking, eating, selfies, loitering, leisure cycling and honking near the tunnel are banned and police checkpoints were set up (whether this is still enforced could not be confirmed). Treat it as a pass-through stop rather than a place to linger, and check the local rules before you go. However, mountain roads are slippery and visibility is poor in rain, which makes the dry season much better.
On weekends riders, cycling groups and traffic to coastal resorts build up congestion, so early weekday mornings are the most comfortable.

items.label: One night of lodging (western Batangas coast)

children.text: Prices are approximate as of
and may vary with local conditions.
There are no restaurants or restrooms around the tunnel, only a small store, so bring drinking water, snacks and tissue. According to one blog, there was a Mountain Brew coffee shop about
3 km
up the road from Ternate selling coffee, cake and sandwiches, so check current information on whether it is open.

For lodging, people generally stay on the western Batangas coast across the tunnel (Nasugbu, Calatagan, Matabungkay and so on) or in Tagaytay, Cavite. Coastal resorts such as Canyon Cove and Hamilo Coast are well known, but check rates and entry conditions before booking.
The tunnel has no lighting, so turn on your headlights even in daytime if you are in a car, and keep a good distance from the rider ahead if you are on a motorcycle.
Since it is close to Manila, leave early in the morning to avoid the congested stretches of Las Piñas, Imus and Dasmariñas.
Take tunnel photos when traffic has cleared, and do not stop or linger on the road inside the tunnel.
There are no restrooms or restaurants, so bring water, snacks and tissue, and charge your phone fully.
One review reports a same-day round trip of over 9 hours, so consider staying a night in Tagaytay or Batangas.
If you plan lunch at a coastal resort or cove, ask in advance whether entry is allowed and what the booking conditions are.
Check your route again at the last minute. Check the latest notices for road works or closures.

The tunnel is very dark because it has no lighting, and reviews say it is dangerous for pedestrians, so do not walk through it, and drivers should turn on their headlights. Also, since March 2021 the Cavite provincial government has declared the tunnel area a no tourism zone that bans parking, selfies, loitering and leisure cycling nearby, so check the current rules.
According to some reviews, guards may stop pedestrians. This is reader-comment level information, so follow instructions on site.
On weekends some motorcycle groups ride with loud exhausts, so watch your speed and following distance.
The roads near the tunnel are mountain roads that can be slippery and foggy in the rain.
There are no restrooms or restaurants and the signal may be weak, so bring what you need in advance.
Private coastal areas and coves such as Hamilo Coast have entry conditions, so do not go in without a reservation.
This is the very mountain the tunnel passes through. It is known for the "parrot's beak" rock at the summit, and you should check the entry procedure before hiking. One article describes it as about
30 minutes
away by car.
Described as a coast with sea views beyond the tunnel. One article says it is now private land under development, so check on site whether access is allowed.
A coastal development area with the Pico de Loro resort, said to be faster to reach once you pass the tunnel. Check usage conditions in advance.
Well-known beaches and resorts on the western Batangas coast. They are often included in itineraries that continue past the tunnel toward Nasugbu.
An alternative route from Manila toward the tunnel and a city used as a base for lodging and meals. It is a good stop if you want to stretch the trip out.
